title: Introduce tethered load-trimmer and circuit guard to reduce noisy reopen storms
author: Avery Chen
description:
Context and motivation:
We observed two production incidents in the last month where tenants experienced brief but severe degradations after circuit reopen storms during an inter-region capacity reflow. Root cause analysis showed rapid circuit state flips combined with indiscriminate admission during reopen windows amplified tail latency and drove eviction waves.

Goal:
Add a lightweight, production-safe mechanism to (1) tie circuit reopen behavior to tenant-level SLO weight (so higher-SLO tenants get less aggressive reopen behavior), and (2) provide a low-overhead load-trimmer that gently sheds low-value tail requests during short overload windows to prevent system-wide oscillation. This should reduce noisy reopen storms and improve recovery stability without broad tenant-impacting hard-shedding.

What this PR changes (high level):
- Introduce a new runtime component: "tethered circuit guard" that maintains per-tenant reopen cooldowns weighted by SLO allocation. The guard exposes a small state machine and backoff window that prevents aggressive reopen attempts for tenants that recently caused overload.
- Add "load_trimmer" admission policy which calculates a probabilistic drop score for new arrivals during short-term overloads based on request token-size, inferred cost, and a tenant-priority multiplier. The algorithm is intentionally conservative (default 2%–10% shed under pressure) and is tunable via feature flags.
- Add feature flags and config knobs: redwood.tethered_circuit_guard.enabled, redwood.load_trimmer.base_shed_pct, redwood.load_trimmer.token_scale. Feature flags default to off for private installs; hosted runs on staged canary.
- Add telemetry: metrics redwood.guard.reopen_attempts, redwood.guard.reopen_suppressed, redwood.trimmer.shed_rate, redwood.trimmer.shed_by_token_bucket and a sparse sampling trace for suppressed reopen paths.
- Small operational runbook (docs/operational/runbook-tethered-guard.md) with rollback steps and golden signal checks.

Design notes and safety considerations:
- Tethering is multiplicative to existing tenant SLO weights; it does not change token billing or permanent limits. It only affects reopen pacing and admission during reopen windows.
- Load trimmer uses a moving-window overload detector before applying shed decisions; it will never run unless overload crosses the configured threshold for >250ms to avoid transient noise.
- All behavior is behind feature flags (hosted: on for us-west-2 canary group; Dedicated/Private: off by default).
- We added a circuit-state audit event that can be correlated to request traces to ensure we can roll back quickly if we observe false positives.

Commits (summary):
- 1) initial: add circuit guard state machine, unit tests
- 2) add load_trimmer admission policy + integration tests
- 3) feature flags, config plumbing, and docs
- 4) fix linting/formatting and add missing metric for tenant-weighted-shed (addressed reviewer feedback)

Files changed (high level):
- src/serving/circuit_guard.go (new) — tethered guard state machine and reconciler
- src/serving/load_trimmer.go (new) — admission policy implementation + lightweight RNG-based shed decision
- pkg/config/flags.go (mod) — feature flags and default values
- docs/operational/runbook-tethered-guard.md (new) — runbook and rollback steps
- tests/unit/circuit_guard_test.go (new) — unit coverage for edge cases
- tests/integration/load_trimmer_it.go (new) — canary-style integration test that simulates reopen storms

Added metrics and traces:
- redwood.guard.reopen_attempts (counter)
- redwood.guard.reopen_suppressed (counter, tagged by tenant_cohort and region)
- redwood.trimmer.shed_rate (gauge)
- redwood.trimmer.shed_by_token_bucket (histogram)

Testing and QA:
- Unit tests added and pass locally.
- Integration test run in benchmark-lab with synthetic reopen storm scenario (5000 req/s for 30s) to validate stable recovery.
- Perf-canary run in us-west-2 for 24h validated no regression in p50/p95 latency for normal traffic; saw 45% reduction in reopen-flip rate for synthetic tenants.
- CI initially failed on commit 2 due to a linting error; fixed in commit 4. Final CI: pass.

Rollout plan:
1) Enable behind feature flag in hosted canary region us-west-2 for 2% of traffic for 6 hours, monitor redwood.guard.reopen_suppressed and p99 latency.
2) Increase to 25% of traffic and run 24h smoke validation.
3) Full region rollout in 48h if metrics are stable.
4) For Dedicated/Private customers, this remains off by default; customers can opt-in by toggling the feature flag via console.

Related work and references:
- Correlates with ENG-1879 (incident RCA) and ENG-1887 (stress test harness updates). See SUP-4021 for a customer-reported symptom that prompted the patch.

Operational runbook highlights (also in docs):
- How to detect a false-positive mass-shed (look for shed_rate spike without corresponding CPU/KV pressure spike).
- Quick rollback: flip redwood.tethered_circuit_guard.enabled=false and disable load_trimmer via redwood.load_trimmer.base_shed_pct=0; both can be done via console feature toggle and take effect immediately.

Notes: this change is intentionally conservative and observability-first. No billing changes, no breaking API changes.

Evan Ross: CI failed lint on 2nd commit, confirmed fix in latest commit and reran canary tests. LGTM.
release_notes: Introduce tethered circuit guard and conservative probabilistic load-trimmer to reduce reopen storms and noisy tenant reopen behavior. Feature-flagged; hosted canary rollout planned. Metrics and runbook included.
testing_notes: Unit tests cover state transitions, weighted cooldowns, and probabilistic shedding boundaries. Integration harness simulates reopen storms with assertable stable recovery. Manual canary validation performed in us-west-2.
rollout_plan: Canary -> staggered ramp -> full region. Feature flags allow immediate rollback. See docs/operational/runbook-tethered-guard.md for playbook.
